Superior? Um, no, I don't really think so. I mean, I'm just a regular guy, you know? I try to treat everyone with respect, whether it's the CEO or the janitor. Actually, the janitor at our building, Marcus, he's a really interesting guy. He used to be a semi-pro bowler back in the nineties. He showed me a picture once of him holding this massive trophy. Bowling is such a weird sport when you think about it. You're just throwing a heavy ball at some pins while wearing shoes that a hundred other people have sweat in. I actually have my own bowling shoes, though. I bought them at a thrift store a few years ago because I went through this phase where I thought my wife and I should join a league. We never did, but the thrift store was amazing. It was one of those huge warehouse ones where they organize everything by color instead of size, which is visually really cool but incredibly frustrating when you're actually trying to find a shirt that fits. It had a dial-up modem, and it made that awful screeching sound every time you tried to connect to the internet. You walk out into the parking lot and the sun is just completely blinding. Bowling is such a weird sport when you think about it. You're just throwing a heavy ball at some pins while wearing shoes that a hundred other people have sweat in. I tried to pick my own stocks once back in the early 2000s. I bought a bunch of shares in this company that made ergonomic desk chairs because I thought, hey, everyone sits at a desk, right?
